title: L2-ARCTIC: a non-native English speech corpus
why_promising: Primary non-native English production from 24 speakers across six L1 groups. Corpus documentation reports 26,867 utterances and 3,599 manually examined/annotated utterances. The manual TextGrids contain words and phones tiers plus error tags/comments, and the spontaneous suitcase subset was annotated by two trained research assistants, cross-checked, and finally checked by the project PI. The release explicitly separates forced-aligned /textgrid files from manual /annotation files, making the qualifying human layer isolatable.
open_question: Authoritative download currently requires accepting license terms and providing name/email/affiliation to receive a link. Before core admission, inspect the authoritative archive/license, inventory only the manual /annotation and suitcase annotation layers, verify that corrected word/phone boundaries are retained source-faithfully, and deduplicate recordings from mirrors or derivative mispronunciation-detection studies.

title: SAIT-EMA: A Tridimensional Electromagnetic Articulography Database for Mandarin with Diverse Language Backgrounds
why_promising: Primary synchronized acoustic and 3D EMA production from 18 Mandarin/L2 Mandarin speakers, with AG501 articulography sampled at 250 Hz and audio at 48 kHz. The Scientific Data descriptor points to a public Zenodo release (10.5281/zenodo.17506802) under CC BY 4.0 and documents raw/processed speaker-level files. This is high-value articulatory production material if a qualifying human-created/corrected segmentation or landmark layer is present.
open_question: Do not admit on instrumentation alone. Inspect the Zenodo file tree and processing documentation for manual or exhaustively human-verified segment/utterance boundaries, labels, landmark corrections, or other qualifying human annotation. If only instrument-generated EMA coordinates and unverified automatic alignment are supplied, exclude from core despite its primary-production provenance.
